evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant women with a suspected small-for-gestational-age (SGA) or growth-restricted fetus: risk screening, ultrasound biometry and Doppler surveillance, and timing of birth. Verified against the Saudi MOH Pocket Manual (small for gestational age chapter, based on RCOG Green-top 31) and NICE NG201.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: RCOG Green-top 31 (cited by MOH) not opened directly
Aspirin prophylaxis for FGR risk not covered here

pathophysiology.summary: SGA describes a fetus or baby with estimated fetal weight or birth weight below the 10th centile (MOH). Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is the subset failing to reach growth potential, usually from placental insufficiency, with risk of hypoxia and stillbirth.
keyMechanisms: Poor placentation (as in pre-eclampsia) reduces uteroplacental blood flow → nutrient and oxygen restriction → reduced growth, especially abdominal circumference.
Rising placental resistance shows as increased umbilical artery pulsatility; absent or reversed end-diastolic flow indicates severe compromise (MOH).
Fetal adaptation redistributes blood to the brain; decompensation is reflected in ductus venosus Doppler and CTG changes.
Constitutionally small but healthy fetuses have normal Doppler.

symptoms: Usually asymptomatic; may present with reduced fetal movements.
History: previous SGA baby, pre-eclampsia, chronic hypertension (MOH).
physicalSigns: Symphysis–fundal height small for dates (more than 3 cm below gestation — MOH).
redFlags: Absent or reversed end-diastolic flow in umbilical artery
Abnormal CTG or reduced fetal movements

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Normal Doppler, steady growth along a low centile.
Structural anomaly or early-onset symmetrical restriction — fetal medicine.

ruleIn.normalValue: Within ±3 cm of gestation in weeks (MOH)

clinicalManagement.title: Screen
actions: Assess risk factors at booking; refer high-risk women for serial ultrasound from 26–28 weeks (MOH).
NICE: FGR risk assessment at booking and in the second trimester; fundal height after 24+0 weeks.

clinicalManagement.title: Surveillance by Doppler (MOH)
actions: Normal umbilical artery Doppler: repeat ultrasound and Doppler every 2 weeks; birth by 37 weeks.
Abnormal Doppler (PI/RI more than 2 SD, end-diastolic flow present): weekly scans; consider birth by 37 weeks.
Absent/reversed end-diastolic flow under 32 weeks: daily umbilical artery and ductus venosus Doppler with CTG; birth by 32 weeks after steroids.

clinicalManagement.title: Birth
actions: Give antenatal corticosteroids if delivering by caesarean section (MOH) — dexamethasone 12 mg IM every 12 h for 2 doses (MOH preterm regimen).
Continuous intrapartum fetal monitoring (see Intrapartum Fetal Compromise topic).

learningObjectives: Detect and monitor a small-for-gestational-age fetus and time birth using Doppler surveillance.

pitfalls: Missing static growth by scanning too often (under 2 weeks apart).
